page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, the x86_64 processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. The instance is configured with 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff between single-threaded and multi-threaded execution. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 945.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU performance of 1108.08, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested instances. Single-threaded gzip compression is poor, registering in the bottom 10% at 19.08 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded workloads leverage the 24 dedicated vCPUs effectively, achieving average tier performance. This is demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 7148.0, a Passmark CPU score of 18444.17, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 83.08 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth remains stable in the average tier, reaching 982.55 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 90.83 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the ecs.sn1ne.6xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for parallelized workloads that do not require high single-core clock speeds or local storage. It is well-suited for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, where it scored 15103.0 on Geekbench clang tests, static web serving at 10.88 GB/sec, and database operations. It can also handle moderate Redis deployments, achieving 16.86 million SET operations per second. However, it is poorly suited for single-threaded processing, memory-intensive databases, or large-scale LLM inference, where text generation for a 7B model is limited to 10.34 tokens per second.
